hook_text: It's bedtime in Kokstad, but your cousin in New York is eating lunch. How?
clip_script: Kokstad, seven at night. Video call to New York: bright sunshine, lunchtime! Grab a globe and a torch. The torch is the Sun. One half lit: day. The other half dark: night. Spin the globe. Kokstad slides into darkness while New York is still in the light. The Earth spins once every 24 hours. The Sun never switches off. We turn away from it!
visual_style: Whiteboard globe lit by a torch, with stickers on Kokstad and New York moving between day and night.
pacing: Puzzle first, then a slow spin of the globe to reveal the answer.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and try the torch and ball test at home.
